overall_summary: Analysis of deduplicated recent uploads reveals that space and extreme planetary scenarios dominate traction. Specifically, 'What If' hypothetical space scenarios and exotic exoplanet conditions (e.g., liquid diamond, burning ice, dark planets) generate the highest views-per-day and engagement metrics (likes-per-view). Content focused on bizarre cosmic environments and planetary physics outperforms abstract psychological facts or standard animal trivia.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) achieved high views (1000+) and strong like ratios relative to older static facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on cinematic hypothetical space survival concepts combining extreme physics with immersive second-person framing.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing bizarre planetary extremes such as Venus having a longer day than year (A9Qa-RmuOr0) or the coal-dark planet TrES-2b (v1rrcZLdp4U) rapidly accumulated over 900-1000 views with strong audience retention signals.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form deep dives into newly discovered or scientifically extreme exoplanets emphasizing bizarre weather or lighting conditions.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head' (ef3ND4qiRHc) or fake memory shorts stagnated below 80 views with minimal engagement.
weak_patterns.action: De-prioritize generic psychology hacks unless framed through a high-stakes neurological mystery or historical anomaly.

weak_patterns.evidence: Simple animal fact statements (e.g., 'Octopuses Have Three Hearts' when repeated or lacking a high-concept narrative twist) showed tapering velocity outside of initial bursts.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal content away from basic trivia toward cinematic animal survival micro-stories or extreme evolutionary anomalies.
